itens.titulo: Micron reports Q4 today: Why Lynx Equity sees massive upside
itens.descricao: Micron reports Q4 today: Why Lynx Equity sees massive upside finance.yahoo.com
trechos: Alongside its Q4 results, Micron will provide critical quarterly guidance that investors are closely watching to gauge the longevity of the AI-driven memory boom.

Lynx analyst KC Rajkumar is projecting a massive revenue path for the semiconductor giant, forecasting top-line sales to reach $525 billion in calendar year 2028 with 80% gross margins, underpinning a decidedly bullish stance.
"Few on the Street made the connection that MU is a beneficiary of Meta's Muse agentic workloads," he wrote in a preview note.

"Over the past few months, the tip of the memory spear has moved from GPU-attached HBM to CPU-attached lpDDR5x as the center of gravity of AI workloads moves from token generation on GPU/XPU to agentic workloads on CPUs," Rajkumar explained.
"Blending in LP-memory puts upward pressure on overall ASP." On the supply side, Lynx identifies a second market misread.

"We think industry giant Samsung has chosen to prioritize elevated profitability over market share, choosing to maintain tight supply even as demand visibility from data centers extends into 2029/2030," Rajkumar wrote.

"This reduces the possibility of a supply glut in 2028/29, a key worry for investors." The prevailing bearish concern heading into today's print is that pricing pressure will mount as DRAM supply loosens in 2028.
The firm maintains its $1,325 price target on Micron but explicitly notes that this figure understates its true conviction.

trechos: "Can gross margins stay up at the rates that they are or do we need to see some normalization so it doesn't feel like, you know, price gouging in a moment?" Bajarin told Yahoo Finance (video above).
"We think demand remains continually strong," he added.
"We still hear DRAM is structurally constrained in many different ways and that's not going away." Micron stock is up 279% this year as of Tuesday's close.

As Yahoo Finance's Brian Sozzi reported, Sur estimates Micron's strategic customer agreements now likely cover 35% or more of its forward bit production, up from roughly 20% of DRAM and a third of NAND volumes disclosed on the last call.
Wall Street expects earnings per share of $31.83 on revenue of $51.49 billion, up 355% from a year ago, according to Bloomberg consensus estimates.
